note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 25-wire topology and the stated rule (p.8 "When any of these switches is activated, the gate closes and remains closed until none of the switches is on.", p.9 "The switch in the middle of the crossing must be so designed that cars passing over it will not close the gate."), not printed; the printed fixture C2/V-EXP7 asserts dial 7 for steps 1-5. ER-29 is prose only, so the wires are as printed. Topology: + on 4Y/5Y/6Y, 4H/5H, 6L, D0; - on 4C/5C/6C, 6H, D7. Relay 4 is set by pushbutton 4 (4X-4F), relay 5 by pushbutton 6 (6X-5F); each holds through its own set-2 N.O. contact (4K-4L, 5K-5L) onto the shared net 4L/5L/5X, which pushbutton 5 or the other held relay keeps at +. Pushbutton 5 alone feeds only that shared net, whose contacts are open, so it closes nothing. Relay 6 follows relay 4 OR relay 5 (4G/5G/6F) and reverses the motor: out, D17 - and D18 +, STOP short on D0; in, D17 + and D18 -, STOP short on D7. Derived: the return to 0 after step 6, pushbutton 5 alone, the right-to-left run (ER-29), a train that enters from the left, stops on pushbutton 5 and backs out, and per-step relay states, including relay 4 still held after step 5 by pushbutton 6 through 5K-5L-4L-4K. Indicator lamps 4-6 are in series with their coils (nC on -) and so follow the relays. Script choices, not printed: 2 s holds per input, 10 s until windows, the back-out sequence 4, 4+5, 4, none. Rest positions c7 and c0 depend on the STOP-short coast (O-R5); direction of travel is not asserted.
